correctness.rationale: The scalar source rule has exactly three branches with boundaries \(a=\lambda\epsilon/h\) and \(\epsilon\). When \(0<\eta h<2\), every branch strictly decreases \(|x|\), and continuity of the induced magnitude map forces the limit to zero. At and above the boundary, exact period-two points exist through \(\eta=2/\lambda\), after which the outer linear multiplier has modulus above one. The cycle interval follows from intersecting the two floor-band constraints on the positive and negative phases.

value.rationale: AGC is introduced specifically to control relative updates and improve stability at larger learning rates, while the positive norm floor is presented as a safeguard for small or zero parameters. The theorem shows that this apparently numerical safeguard can determine the exact asymptotic stability threshold: any positive floor restores raw curvature near the optimum and creates a full bounded two-cycle band across the nominal gap between raw and clipped curvature ceilings. This is a sharp structural diagnostic of when AGC can control transient relative steps without enlarging universal local stability.
